The Afdeling bestuursrechtspraak van de Raad van State is the highest general administrative court of the Netherlands. It decides at the highest instance on disputes between citizens and government and between government bodies, and hears immigration cases on appeal.

The College ter Beoordeling van Geneesmiddelen (CBG-MEB) is the Dutch medicines authority. It assesses and monitors medicines for humans and animals, grants marketing authorisations and tracks adverse effects.

The Agentschap van de Generale Thesaurie (Dutch State Treasury Agency) is part of the Ministry of Finance. It finances the state by managing the national debt and public money in the treasury and by organising central government payments.

The Algemene Bestuursdienst (ABD) is part of the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations. It recruits and places senior civil servants in leadership positions across central government and develops their leadership.
High Council of State that audits the revenue and expenditure of the central government (het Rijk) and reports on them to the government and the Staten-Generaal.

The Auditdienst Rijk is the internal controlling auditor of the ministries. It audits financial processes within departments so they can present an approved internal audit statement when the Algemene Rekenkamer carries out its inspections.
The Belastingdienst assesses and collects taxes, customs duties and excise for the state. It falls organisationally under the Ministry of Finance.

It collects fines and administrative costs such as traffic fines, as well as other court-imposed monetary penalties and damages. It has existed since 1990, after the Wahv took effect.
Independent planning bureau that produces economic forecasts and analyses for the cabinet and for the preparation of the national budget.

The Centrale Raad van Beroep is one of the four highest administrative courts and rules on appeal in cases on social insurance, social provisions and civil service matters. The Raad is based in Utrecht.
CIBG is an implementing organisation of the Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport. It assesses, registers and provides data, such as the Donor Register, often under statutory tasks.

Body of the Kingdom that supervises the application of the budget standards by Curaçao and Sint Maarten; the council of ministers of the Kingdom decides on the appointment of the members (Rijkswet financieel toezicht Curaçao en Sint Maarten art. 2 and 4).

The College van Beroep voor het bedrijfsleven is the highest administrative court in economic administrative law and sits in Den Haag. Among other things, it hears cases on competition, market regulation, subsidies, fertilisers and financial supervision.

The Dienst Financieel-Economische Integriteit (DFEI) is a self-contained supervisory authority within the Ministry of Finance. It promotes integrity among gatekeepers and entrepreneurs and combats financial-economic crime in European and Caribbean Netherlands.

Dienst ICT Uitvoering (DICTU) is an ICT service provider of central government, part of the Ministry of Economic Affairs. It develops and manages over 1,500 applications, including for subsidies and identity management.

The Dienst Identificatie en Screening Asielzoekers (DISA) identifies and registers asylum seekers on behalf of the minister. Its staff use the powers that the Vreemdelingenwet 2000 gives the minister.

The Dienst Justitiële Inrichtingen (DJI) falls under the Ministry of Justice and Security. It provides daily care for adults and young people in its institutions and works with them on reintegration, at about 50 locations.

The Dienst Publiek en Communicatie (DPC) is part of the Ministry of General Affairs. It advises and supports all departments in their communication with society, including campaigns, online services and research.

The Dienst Terugkeer en Vertrek (DT&V) implements Dutch return policy. It arranges the departure of foreigners with no right of residence, such as failed asylum seekers. It has been operational since January 2007 and falls under the Ministry of Asylum and Migration.

Dienst Toeslagen pays out income-dependent benefits: rent, health care, childcare and the child-related budget. Since 01-01-2021 it has been an independent directorate-general of the Ministry of Finance. The benefits rest on the Algemene wet inkomensafhankelijke regelingen (Awir).

Dienst Uitvoering Onderwijs (DUO) carries out tasks for the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science. It handles student finance, tuition payments, student travel products, diploma services and state examinations, and processes repayment of student debt.

Dienst Uitvoering Subsidies aan Instellingen (DUS-I) processes subsidy applications and manages funding schemes for the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and the Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport.

The Huurcommissie is an impartial, independent dispute resolver for tenants and landlords. It assesses disputes over rent, maintenance and service costs, among other things, under the law and issues binding decisions.

The Dienst van het Koninklijk Huis supports the King, Queen Máxima and Princess Beatrix in their work and private lives. The service also supports the other members of the Royal House in their duties. Its nearly 300 staff work in Den Haag, Amsterdam, Apeldoorn and Baarn; the grootmeester (Grand Master) heads the royal household.

The Algemene Inlichtingen- en Veiligheidsdienst (AIVD) is the Dutch intelligence and security service, part of the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations. It protects the Netherlands and democracy against national and international threats and works under the Wet op de inlichtingen- en veiligheidsdiensten.

Domeinen Roerende Zaken (DRZ) falls under the Ministry of Finance. It manages goods seized by authorities and processes surplus central government goods. Proceeds from auctions go to the treasury or to crime victims.

The Douane (customs) is part of the Ministry of Finance. It handles imports, exports, tariffs, excise duties and customs declarations and checks goods flows for safety, health, economic and environmental compliance.

The Senate's Foreign Affairs, Defence and Development Cooperation Committee prepares the written consideration of bills on Foreign Affairs, Defence and Development Cooperation, such as international treaties, military pensions, the employment terms of military personnel and military criminal law and procedure.

The Senate's Interior Committee prepares the written consideration of bills on the Interior, General Affairs and the Royal House, such as administrative boundaries, voting rights, the civil service and revisions of the Constitution. It also prepares the consideration of the budgets of the Interior, General Affairs and the King's Household.

The Senate's Digitalisation Committee prepares the written consideration of bills setting standards for digitalisation. It consults the subject committees on the consideration of (European) legislation in that field.

The Senate's European Affairs Committee prepares the written consideration of bills on European cooperation, such as European treaties. It can consult on this with the Minister of Foreign Affairs responsible for European cooperation.

The Senate's Economic Affairs / Climate and Green Growth Committee prepares the consideration of bills on economic affairs, energy, innovation, competition and consumer policy, entrepreneurship, telecommunications, postal services and statistics.
The Senate's Finance Committee prepares the consideration of financial bills, mainly on taxation, customs, payments and banking.
The Commissie voor de Geloofsbrieven is a committee of the Eerste Kamer. It examines the credentials of newly appointed members before they take their seats.

The Senate's Immigration & Asylum / JHA Council Committee prepares the consideration of bills on immigration, integration and asylum. It also considers proposals that come before the Council of Justice and Home Affairs ministers of the European Union (the JHA Council).
The Senate's Infrastructure, Water Management, Housing and Spatial Planning Committee prepares the written consideration of bills on infrastructure, water management, housing and spatial planning.

The Senate's Justice and Security Committee prepares the written consideration of bills on justice and security, such as private law including family law, criminal law, the enforcement of sentences and legal aid.

The Senate's Kingdom Relations Committee prepares the written consideration of bills on the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom and of Kingdom acts. It discusses the policy of the ministers responsible for Kingdom relations and keeps in contact with the elected representatives of Aruba, Curaçao, Sint Maarten, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba.

The Senate's Agriculture, Nature and Food Quality Committee prepares the consideration of bills on agriculture and horticulture, fisheries, food quality, animal welfare and animal health, nature and biodiversity, and nitrogen.
The Senate's Education, Culture and Science Committee prepares the written consideration of bills on education, culture and science, and on the media.
The Senate's Social Affairs and Employment Committee prepares the written consideration of bills on social affairs, such as social security, working conditions, employment services and integration.
The Senate's Petitions Committee examines the petitions sent to the Senate and reports on them.
The Senate's Health, Welfare and Sport Committee prepares the written consideration of bills on public health, welfare and sport.

The Eerste Kamer is the indirectly elected part of the Staten-Generaal. It has 75 members, elected by the members of the Provinciale Staten and the electoral colleges, and it reviews the bills that the Tweede Kamer has passed.

Geneeskundige Gezondheidsdienst Zuid-Limburg is the municipal public health service (GGD) of 16 municipalities in the region of Veiligheidsregio Zuid-Limburg, which set it up together by a joint arrangement. A director of public health heads the service.

The Hoge Raad der Nederlanden is the highest court in civil, criminal and tax cases. It is a court of cassation: it assesses whether lower courts applied the law correctly and whether the procedure was followed correctly. The Hoge Raad is also the court of cassation for Aruba, Curacao, Sint Maarten and Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba.
The Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst (IND) handles applications for residence permits and nationality. It also carries out asylum procedures and family reunification cases.

The Inspecteur-Generaal der Krijgsmacht (IGK) advises the Minister of Defence on all matters affecting the armed forces, carries out investigations and mediates in individual cases. The IGK is also inspector for veterans and reservists.

The Inspectie belastingen, toeslagen en douane has been an independent part of the Ministry of Finance since 01-01-2022. It signals and investigates problems in the services of the Belastingdienst, Dienst Toeslagen and Douane and sends its reports to both Houses.

The Inspectie Gezondheidszorg en Jeugd (IGJ) falls under the Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport. It supervises the quality and safety of care and youth assistance and investigates complaints through the Landelijk Meldpunt Zorg.

The Inspectie Justitie en Veiligheid falls under the Ministry of Justice and Security. It supervises, among others, the police, prisons, juvenile justice institutions, migration services and fire brigades.

The Inspectie Leefomgeving en Transport (ILT) falls under the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management. It supervises safety and sustainability in areas such as waste, drinking water, aviation, rail, shipping, freight transport and housing corporations.

The Inspectie Militaire Gezondheidszorg (IMG) is an independent supervisory body within the Ministry of Defence. It oversees the quality of military healthcare, including during deployments. It reports directly to the secretary-general.

The Inspectie Overheidsinformatie en Erfgoed falls under the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science. It supervises archaeology, protected cultural heritage, the national collection and the accessibility of government information, including under the Archiefwet.

The Inspectie van het Onderwijs falls under the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science. It supervises the quality of education and publishes inspection reports and, each year, De Staat van het Onderwijs.
The Inspectie Veiligheid Defensie (IVD) has been an independent supervisor of physical and social safety at Defence since 2018. It carries out incident, thematic and systemic investigations.
Consultation of four parliamentary delegations: the Staten of Aruba, of Curaçao and of Sint Maarten and the Staten-Generaal, with members of the Eerste and the Tweede Kamer.

The Interprovinciaal Overleg (IPO) is the partnership of the twelve provinces. Through it the provinces pool knowledge and contacts and represent their shared interests with the government, parliament and other partners.

Justis is the screening authority of the Ministry of Justice and Security. It is the only organisation in the Netherlands that issues the Verklaring Omtrent het Gedrag (VOG) and also handles, among other things, weapons permits and private security licences.

The Justitiële ICT Organisatie (JIO) is the ICT service provider of the Ministry of Justice and Security. It supplies hardware, software, applications and secure cloud environments for workplaces across the Netherlands.

The Justitiële Informatiedienst (Justid) falls under the Ministry of Justice and Security. It manages and provides justice data, such as criminal records and identity checks, to partners in the criminal, migration and youth justice chains.

The Kabinet Minister-President (KMP) is part of the Ministry of General Affairs. It advises and supports the prime minister, runs the secretariat of the Council of Ministers and prepares decision-making.

The Kabinet van de Koning supports the King in carrying out his constitutional duties. It handles and prepares the King's contacts with the minister-president and the other ministers and state secretaries. It processes the laws, general administrative orders and royal decrees presented for signature and handles petitions from citizens.

The cabinet consists of the ministers and the state secretaries. The ministers and the state secretaries are appointed and dismissed by royal decree. The current kabinet-Jetten was sworn in on 23 February 2026 and has 18 ministers and 10 state secretaries.

The Kanselarij der Nederlandse Orden houses and supports the Kapittel voor de Civiele Orden and the Kapittel der Militaire Willems-Orde in their advice on proposals for decorations. The organisation manages the insignia, keeps registers of decorated persons and guards the purity and dignity of the orders. Its history goes back to 1815, when the Militaire Willems-Orde and the Orde van de Nederlandse Leeuw were established; the Kanselier der Nederlandse Orden is at its head.
The persons entitled to vote for the Tweede Kamer: Dutch nationals aged eighteen and over who are not excluded from the right to vote. They elect the 150 members of the Tweede Kamer.

The Kiesraad is responsible for elections in the Netherlands and ensures that they are fair and transparent. Statutory task: The Kiesraad has the following tasks:* advising the government and both Kamers der Staten-Generaal on technical implementation matters concerning the right to vote or elections (article A2 Kieswet);* acting as the central electoral committee for the elections of the members of:
a. the Tweede Kamer (article E II, second paragraph, Kieswet);
b. the Eerste Kamer (article S I, first paragraph, Kieswet);
c. the European Parliament (article Y9, first paragraph, Kieswet);* advising government bodies, political parties, media and citizens during elections and acting as an expert adviser in legal proceedings.

The Koninklijk Nederlands Meteorologisch Instituut (KNMI) falls under the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management. It provides independent knowledge, advice and warnings on weather, climate and seismology.
Logius is a digital service provider of the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations. It provides services for the whole public sector, such as DigiD, eHerkenning, Digipoort and MijnOverheid.

The Militaire Inlichtingen- en Veiligheidsdienst (MIVD) is the military intelligence service, part of the Ministry of Defence, established in 2002. It gathers foreign military intelligence, carries out security screenings and works under the Wet op de inlichtingen- en veiligheidsdiensten 2017.

The Militaire Luchtvaart Autoriteit (MLA) has been an independent supervisor within the Ministry of Defence since 01-07-2005. On behalf of the minister it sets rules for military aviation safety, certifies people, equipment and organisations and supervises compliance.

The Ministerie van Sociale Ontwikkeling, Arbeid & Welzijn is one of the nine ministries of the country of Curaçao. The ministerie van Algemene Zaken coordinates government policy and central government communication and safeguards their unity and continuity. It supports the minister-president in preparing and carrying out cabinet policy. The ministry was established by royal decree of 3 July 1937 and is based in Den Haag.

The ministerie van Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties works on democracy, public administration, fundamental rights, housing and spatial planning, and on relations within the Kingdom. Since the departmental reorganisation of 23 February 2026, public housing, spatial planning and digital affairs also fall within the department. The ministry is based in Den Haag.

The ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken coordinates and carries out the foreign policy of the Netherlands, from Den Haag and through embassies, consulates and other missions in about 150 countries. It promotes Dutch interests, contributes to international stability and helps Dutch nationals abroad. The department has existed since 1798.

The ministerie van Defensie protects the security of the Netherlands and its allies and contributes to the international legal order and stability. The armed forces also support society during disasters and crises. The department consists of the central staff in Den Haag and the operational units of the navy, army and air force, the marechaussee and supporting commands.

The ministerie van Economische Zaken en Klimaat works towards a productive, resilient and sustainable economy. The department is responsible for entrepreneurship, innovation, climate and energy, digitalisation and the management of raw materials. On 23 February 2026 its name changed from Economische Zaken to Economische Zaken en Klimaat; tasks in the fields of climate, green growth and the circular economy were transferred to it at that time.

The ministerie van Financiën manages the public finances and is responsible for financially sound central government. It draws up the Rijksbegroting, is responsible for the tax system and supervises the financial sector. The ministry has existed since 1798, which makes it one of the oldest departments.

The ministerie van Infrastructuur en Waterstaat works on accessibility, safe dikes and clean air, soil and water. The department is responsible for the road, rail and water networks and for the management of Rijkswaterstaat. It also works towards a good living environment and the economical use of raw materials.

The ministerie van Justitie en Veiligheid is responsible for the legal order and for a safer and more just society. It works with municipalities, the Openbaar Ministerie, the police and other partners on law enforcement, protection and migration. Since 23 February 2026, asylum and migration also fall within this department.

The ministerie van Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur works for sustainable and safe food, healthy nature and a vital countryside. The department focuses on agriculture, fisheries, food security, nature and nitrogen, for current and future generations. It is based in Den Haag.

The ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap ensures good education, room for science and a free cultural sector. It sets frameworks for and funds education and culture policy and science. The department has had its current name since 2003, when it moved from Zoetermeer to Den Haag.

The ministerie van Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid works for fair, healthy and safe work and for financial security for everyone. It is responsible for social security, the labour market and income policy. The ministry is based in Den Haag.

The ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport works for good and affordable care and support. It encourages a healthy lifestyle, sufficient exercise and sport and is responsible for the healthcare system. The department is based in Den Haag.

The Ministerie van Verkeer, Vervoer & Ruimtelijke Planning is one of the nine ministries of the country of Curaçao. According to the government of Curaçao, it is responsible for the sustainable development of traffic, transport and urban planning.

Together the ministers form the ministerraad and deliberate and decide on general government policy. The minister-president is chair and promotes the unity of that policy. The council meets in principle weekly, chaired by the minister-president.

The Nationaal Archief is an agency of the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science. It is the General State Archive and preserves and opens up the archives of central government, under the Archiefwet.

The Nationaal Coördinator Groningen (NCG) works on recovery in the Groningen earthquake area. It has buildings inspected and reinforced and offers financial support, temporary housing and damage compensation.

The Nationaal Cyber Security Centrum (NCSC) falls under the Ministry of Justice and Security. It strengthens organisations' digital resilience with security advisories, incident support and registration under the NIS2 rules.
Hoog College van Staat that investigates complaints about the government and informs the Tweede Kamer annually of its findings.

The Nationale Opvang Organisatie (NOO) is a temporary task organisation, set up by decision of the Minister of Justice and Security of 15-06-2022. It arranges sufficient reception locations and basic services for displaced persons from Ukraine and implements the related funding schemes.

The Nederlands Forensisch Instituut (NFI) falls under the Ministry of Justice and Security. Under the Regeling taken NFI it carries out independent forensic case investigation, develops new examination methods and serves as a national and international expertise centre.

The Nederlandse Arbeidsinspectie falls under the Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment. It supervises labour laws and social security, investigates workplace accidents, combats fraud and has its own criminal investigation division.

The Nederlandse Emissieautoriteit (NEa) is the independent national authority for the implementation and supervision of market instruments that contribute to a climate-neutral society. The NEa is a so-called small independent administrative body (zbo). This means that the board is a zbo, while the working organisation is an agency of the Ministerie van Economische Zaken en Klimaat (EZK). The main clients of the organisation are the ministries of EZK, Infrastructuur en Waterstaat (IenW) and Financiën (MinFin). The NEa is based in Den Haag and has more than 140 employees.

Statutory task: Supports the implementation of emissions trading (greenhouse gases) and, as an independent supervisor, checks compliance with the rules on greenhouse gases.

The Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit (NVWA) falls under the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature. It supervises the safety of food and consumer products, animal welfare and nature protection.

The Netherlands Foreign Investment Agency (NFIA) is an operational unit of the Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland, under the responsibility of the Ministry of Economic Affairs. It promotes the Netherlands as a business location and supports foreign companies that want to establish or expand here.

Government of the country of Sint Maarten. The Kingdom comprises the countries of Nederland, Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten (Statuut voor het Koninkrijk art. 1).

The government is formed by the King and the ministers. The King is inviolable; the ministers are responsible for government policy. The kabinet-Jetten, formed by D66, VVD and CDA, was sworn in on 23 February 2026 and has 18 ministers and 10 state secretaries.

The Rijksacademie voor Financiën, Economie en Bedrijfsvoering is part of the Ministry of Finance. It offers training courses, trainee programmes and tailored programmes for central government civil servants, and trains foreign civil servants.

The Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed is an executive organisation of the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science. It works on archaeology, collections, monuments and landscape and keeps the Rijksmonumentenregister (national monuments register).

The Rijksdienst voor Identiteitsgegevens is an agency of the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations. Among other things it manages the Basisregistratie Personen (personal records database) and the systems for travel documents and citizen service numbers.

The Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland is an agency of the Ministry of Economic Affairs. On behalf of ministries, local authorities and the European Union it carries out subsidy and other schemes for entrepreneurs.

The Rijksinkoopsamenwerking (RIS) is a shared service organisation for procurement within the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations. It buys on behalf of several ministries and runs government-wide tenders for cleaning and for travel and accommodation.

The Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur supervises the availability, continuity and reliability of IT and communication networks. It enforces rules, strengthens digital resilience and issues permits and registrations for certain equipment. It falls under the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

The Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu (RIVM, National Institute for Public Health and the Environment) falls under the Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport. It researches and monitors public health and the living environment and advises the government, including on infectious diseases, population screening and the environment.

The council of ministers of the Kingdom consists of the ministers appointed by the King and the Gevolmachtigde Ministers of Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten, who act on behalf of the government of their country (Statuut art. 7 and 8).

The Rijksorganisatie Beveiliging en Logistiek falls under the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations. It provides state security (Rijksbeveiliging), including at critical state sites, and state logistics (Rijkslogistiek), including the vehicle fleet.

The Rijksorganisatie voor Informatiehuishouding is the centre of expertise and services for the central government in information management. It falls under the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations and runs projects, programmes and knowledge networks.

The Rijksorganisatie voor Ontwikkeling, Digitalisering en Innovatie (ODI) falls under the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations. It temporarily reinforces government bodies on complex issues with expertise in organisational development, digitalisation and innovation.

The Rijksvastgoedbedrijf falls under the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations. It manages and develops the State's real estate and land, such as offices, courthouses, defence sites and monuments, and leases or sells it.

The Kingdom Representative for the public bodies Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba reports to the ministers concerned on matters affecting the three public bodies. Among other things the representative approves appointments of island civil servants and is accountable to the minister concerned.

The Rijksvoorlichtingsdienst (RVD, Government Information Service) is part of the Ministry of General Affairs. It handles communications for the prime minister and the cabinet and for the Royal House, and chairs the Communications Council (VoRa).

Rijkswaterstaat is part of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management. It manages and maintains the national roads, waterways and main water system and works on the living environment, energy and climate.

This is a cluster consisting of independent administrative bodies (zbo's) that do not fall under the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen. The underlying parts of this cluster are therefore not named in the Register van Overheidsorganisaties. This cluster consists of both private-law and public-law organisations.

Funded green education institutions provide agricultural and nature education and receive funding for it from the Ministry of Agriculture. They count as a legal entity with a statutory task (rwt) under the Comptabiliteitswet 2016.

Funded primary education institutions are school boards that provide primary and special education and receive state funding for it. The Wet op het primair onderwijs regulates their tasks, funding and governance.

Funded secondary education institutions are school boards that provide vmbo, havo and vwo education and receive state funding for it. The Wet voortgezet onderwijs 2020 regulates their funding and governance. The earlier Wet op het voortgezet onderwijs was repealed in 2022.

Funded institutions for higher professional education are the universities of applied sciences that receive state funding. The Wet op het hoger onderwijs en wetenschappelijk onderzoek regulates their funding, admission, accreditation and governance.

Funded institutions for secondary vocational education include the regional training centres and vocational schools that receive state funding. The Wet educatie en beroepsonderwijs regulates vocational education and adult education, their funding and governance.

Funded institutions for academic education are the universities that receive state funding. The Wet op het hoger onderwijs en wetenschappelijk onderzoek regulates their funding, admission, accreditation and governance.

The Stichting Centraal Orgaan Voorraadvorming Aardolieproducten (COVA) is a legal entity with a statutory task. COVA is the central, independent organisation that holds strategic oil stocks for the Netherlands on behalf of the minister of Klimaat en Groene Groei. The mandatory oil stock consists of at most 2/3 crude oil and at least 1/3 refined product. The product stock consists of petrol, diesel and kerosene, divided in proportion to domestic use.

The Commissie voor de milieueffectrapportage is an independent advisory body, established in 1986. It advises competent authorities on environmental impact assessments. Article 17.5 of the Omgevingswet regulates the establishment of the commission.

The Depositogarantiefonds is the fund within the deposit guarantee scheme, which De Nederlandsche Bank runs on behalf of the government. If a bank fails, it pays out up to 100,000 euro per depositor per bank. The banks pay into the fund.

Distributors of electricity and drinking water on Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba supply these utilities under the Wet elektriciteit en drinkwater BES. The act regulates production and distribution through permits and designations under ACM supervision.

Examining institutions are bodies that the minister designates under article 19 of the Examenregeling frequentiegebruik 2008 to conduct examinations. A designation lasts at most five years and is not transferable.

FMO is the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. It invests in entrepreneurs in more than 85 countries in developing and emerging economies and is supervised by De Nederlandsche Bank. The State is one of its shareholders.

Gezondheidsdienst voor Dieren B.V. (Royal GD) in Deventer combats and prevents contagious animal diseases. It monitors animal health, carries out mandatory disease control programmes for the government and runs a veterinary laboratory.

Havenbedrijf Amsterdam NV develops and manages the Amsterdam port area and its infrastructure. Its harbour master division regulates and enforces shipping traffic in the North Sea Canal area. Shareholders were not established in the sources.

Havenbedrijf Rotterdam NV develops and manages the Rotterdam port area and ensures smooth and safe shipping. Its shareholders are the municipality of Rotterdam (70.8 percent) and the State (29.2 percent). The harbour master also acts as rijkshavenmeester.
Het Juridisch Loket gives citizens free legal advice and refers them on. The Wet op de rechtsbijstand regulates state-funded legal aid for people with insufficient financial means.

The HISWA-vereniging is a trade association of recognised water sports businesses. The Algemene Rekenkamer lists it as a legal entity with a statutory task (rwt) under the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management.

The Inlichtingenbureau (IB) is a foundation established in 2001 with a statutory task under the Wet SUWI. It acts as a data hub for municipalities and supports them in carrying out, among other things, the Participatiewet. It falls under the Ministry of Social Affairs.

The Innovam Branche Kwalificatie Instituut (IBKI) is responsible for developing and administering theory and practical exams in the mobility sector, for example for people who want to obtain or keep the authority to carry out a periodic vehicle inspection (APK) of motor vehicles. IBKI is a trade name of the [Stichting Vakopleiding Automobiel- en Motorrijwielbedrijf (VAM)](https://organisaties.overheid.nl/30133473/Stichting_VAM__Opleidingsinstituur_voor_het_Motorvoertuig-__Tweewieler-_en_Aanverwant_Bedrijf), also known as Innovam.

These are institutions that the minister charges with managing the State's museum cultural property under article 2.8 of the Erfgoedwet. The minister considers expertise, suitable facilities and public accessibility.
Invest International B.V. was established in 2021 under the Machtigingswet oprichting Invest International. The State holds 51 percent of the shares and FMO 49 percent.
Invest-NL is a financing and development institution in which the State holds all shares. It was established under the Machtigingswet oprichting Invest-NL and has been active since 16-01-2020.

On behalf of the Minister of Infrastructure and Water Management, Kiwa Register B.V. issues permits for professional transport by sea, inland waterway and road. The Algemene Rekenkamer lists it as a legal entity with a statutory task.

Classification bureaus are private organisations that the minister designates under article 6 of the Schepenbesluit 1965. They set technical rules for the construction and equipment of ships. Ships may comply with them as an alternative to the government requirements.

National broadcasting organisations produce the national public media offering together with the NPO. The Mediawet 2008 regulates the public media task, the NPO as steering and cooperation body, and the recognised broadcasters.

Stichting Leger des Heils Jeugdbescherming & Reclassering carries out child protection, juvenile probation and adult probation. It is one of the 16 certified institutions and one of three probation organisations in the Netherlands.

Pilotage guides seagoing vessels in Dutch waters. The Loodsenwet regulates the Dutch pilot corporation and regional pilot corporations of registered pilots. Nederlands Loodswezen B.V. supports the pilots, collects the fees and arranges transport to the ships.

VSL is the national metrology institute of the Netherlands. It manages primary measurement standards and reference materials. The Metrologiewet lets the minister designate an institution for the national measurement standard. TNO is the shareholder.

The Nationaal Resolutiefonds (legally the Afwikkelingsfonds) was established in 2015. De Nederlandsche Bank can use it as national resolution authority to finance resolution measures. Articles 3a:72 and 3a:74 of the Wft regulate the fund.

The Nationale Politie is the national police force of article 25 of the Politiewet 2012, with regional units, national units and support services. The police maintain the legal order and help those who need help, under the competent authority.

The Nederlands Bureau Motorrijtuigverzekeraars (NBM) acts when foreign vehicles cause damage in the Netherlands and Dutch vehicles cause damage abroad. It works closely with the Waarborgfonds Motorverkeer, which is financed from motor liability premiums.

The Nederlandse Omroep Stichting (NOS) is a public broadcaster that provides news, sport and major events. The Mediawet 2008 regulates its position in the national public media system alongside the NPO.

Neth-ER is an association founded in Brussels in 2006 by eleven Dutch organisations in education, research and innovation. It seeks to influence European policy on behalf of the Dutch knowledge community. The Rekenkamer lists it under the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science.

Private forensic psychiatric centres are non-state institutions for the care of people under a tbs order. They fall under the Beginselenwet verpleging ter beschikking gestelden and the Wet forensische zorg, with a supervisory committee.

Private judicial youth institutions are institutions designated by the minister for the accommodation and treatment of young people in youth detention. The Beginselenwet justitiële jeugdinrichtingen (article 3b) regulates their status, governance and subsidy.

ProRail is the railway infrastructure manager. This means that we are responsible for the maintenance, renewal, expansion and safety of the Dutch railway network. As an independent party we allocate the capacity on 7,000 kilometres of track, manage all train traffic (160 million kilometres per year) and build and manage stations. We do this with attention to our society and with an eye to the future. ProRail stands for sustainable mobility. Through innovation we make it possible for more people to travel by train and for more goods to be transported by rail. ProRail is an unlisted company. The company's board consists of three statutory directors. The supervisory board oversees it. The Dutch State, through Railinfratrust B.V., is the sole shareholder of ProRail B.V. The shareholding is held by the ministry of Infrastructuur en Waterstaat.

The Raad stands for a safe and just society. To that end, the Raad contributes to the quality of law enforcement by supervising, from an independent position, the functioning of the justice chain and providing insight into it.
Regional public media institutions provide public media services for a specific region. Title 2.3 of the Mediawet 2008 (articles 2.60a to 2.74) regulates their tasks and designation.

Rendac Son B.V. carries out the statutory task of collecting, transporting and processing carcasses and category 1 and 2 animal by-products. The Wet dieren obliges holders to offer them to Rendac. The Ministry of Agriculture, Nature and Food Quality concludes the agreement.

Inclusive education partnerships in primary education adopt a support plan at least every four years, distribute support funds among schools and assess admission to special education. Article 18a of the Wet op het primair onderwijs regulates this.

Regional partnerships that secondary schools must join under the Wet passend onderwijs. They adopt a support plan every four years and, since 01-01-2025, must set up a parent and youth support centre.

The organisation is subsidised by, among others, DGPJS. Slachtofferhulp Nederland stands up for the interests and rights of victims of a crime or a traffic accident. At the 75 Buro's Slachtofferhulp, 1500 volunteers and 250 professionals work every day to help victims. The services consist of practical and legal advice and emotional support. In the media and in politics, Slachtofferhulp Nederland acts as an advocate. The organisation encourages research and lobbies politically with the aim of strengthening the position of victims.

Foundation that has managed, on behalf of the State, the shares in nationalised financial institutions, such as ABN AMRO and ASN Bank, since 01-07-2011. The Minister of Finance decides on share sales; NLFI advises him.

Independent foundation that gives expert advice, solely at the request of the administrative court, in disputes about the physical environment. It was formed in 1996 by merging two government offices.

Foundation that collects waste from professional inland shipping through a national network of reception facilities, and issues and checks sailing documents. It was set up in the early 1990s as the national institute under the Ship Waste Convention.

Foundation in Arnhem that develops, on behalf of the government, the statutory tests and exams for primary, secondary and vocational education (Centrale Toetsen en Examens division). The CitoLab division does research and innovation.

Defensie protects what we Dutch hold dear. We fight for a world in which people can live in freedom and safety, because we are convinced that every person deserves that. That is our mission, and for that we go on missions. The armed forces have 3 main tasks. These are: protecting our own territory and that of allies; promoting the (international) legal order and stability; supporting civil authorities and providing assistance in disasters and crises.

Research component of Wageningen University & Research, now Stichting Wageningen Research, which grew out of the Dienst Landbouwkundig Onderzoek. It does applied research for government, industry and non-profit organisations; the agriculture ministry funds it.

The College donorgegevens kunstmatige bevruchting (Cdkb) carries out the Wet donorgegevens kunstmatige bevruchting. Since 2004, the data of sperm, egg and embryo donors have been registered nationally. The Cdkb is responsible for managing these data and provides them on request to the donor child, the parents or the general practitioner. The board of the Cdkb has transferred a number of implementing tasks to the Centraal Informatiepunt Beroepen Gezondheidszorg (CIBG), including the registration of donor data, the secretariat of the Cdkb and the provision of information. The Cdkb nevertheless is and remains responsible for the data and decides on requests for donor data that it receives. The CIBG is an agency of the Ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport (VWS).

Foundation that has sold advertising time on public radio, television and digital channels since 1965. The revenue goes to the Ministry of OCW, which funds public broadcasting. Advertising may not exceed 10 percent of broadcast time per year or 15 percent per day.

About Halt: Halt focuses on preventing, combating and punishing youth crime. Halt has the statutory task of punishing transgressive behaviour by young people. About 17,000 young people a year receive a Halt penalty. Halt is also active in prevention. Halt gives many information sessions at schools, sports clubs or in the neighbourhood. Halt also offers tailored interventions and projects. Halt is a connecting partner between the family, the world of juvenile criminal law, the municipality and organisations that young people deal with. In this way Halt actively contributes to a safe and liveable environment. Organisation: since 1 January 2013, Halt has been one organisation with teams throughout the country. In this way Halt continues to meet local wishes. Halt joins forces into one vital organisation that has more clout and works efficiently. Halt is a foundation with a director/board member and a supervisory board. The organisation consists of regional teams (in line with the judicial map and the 10 police regions) and a national office, each with a team manager. Funding: Halt carries out the Halt penalty under the responsibility of the Openbaar Ministerie. The ministry of Veiligheid en Justitie funds the execution of the Halt penalty. Halt carries out prevention assignments on behalf of municipalities and other clients, such as central government, provinces, care and welfare organisations, sports federations and schools. TASK: preventing, combating and punishing transgressive behaviour by young people.

National curriculum development centre for primary, special and secondary education. SLO works for the Ministry of OCW and develops national core objectives, exam programmes and sample materials together with schools.

Private-law foundation that builds, maintains and manages the Leidingenstraat, an underground corridor of about 80 kilometres between the industrial areas of Rotterdam and Antwerp, with branches to Moerdijk and Vlissingen. Petrochemical and utility companies lay pipes and cables there.

National public broadcaster without members, with statutory tasks under the Mediawet for background journalism, arts and culture, youth, education and minorities. NTR has existed since 2010, after the merger of NPS, Teleac and RVU.

TASK: offering programmes aimed at resocialisation, like the two partners mentioned earlier, to people who have come into contact with the justice system. Deploying expertise and manpower to prevent repeat offences. It acts as quickly as possible, preferably immediately after someone has been arrested. It can play a role in all phases of the legal process. The Reclassering carries out three core tasks: investigation, information and reporting to the justice authorities on the person of the offender and the circumstances of the offending behaviour. That information can play a role in the further handling of the case by the justice system; guidance and supervision. Guidance and supervision can be carried out either voluntarily or in a mandatory framework (judgment). The Reclassering carries out activities that enable the suspect to better handle his responsibility in society; offering early assistance to detainees; offering reintegration programmes to detainees; developing and offering community sentences and penitentiary programmes. Community sentences can be divided into work and learning sentences. They are imposed by the judge, and the probation service provides organisation and guidance. When taking part in a penitentiary programme, a detainee spends the last part of his prison sentence outside the walls of the institution, in his home environment, under strict guidance and supervision. In this way the detainee slowly learns to deal with an increasing degree of freedom. Explanation: the stichting Reclassering Nederland (SRN) was founded in 1995 and brings together all institutions engaged in probation work in the Netherlands, namely: Stichting Reclassering Nederland, the probation department of the Leger des Heils, and the addiction care institutions united in GGZ Nederland. The bundling of probation work was started to safeguard the quality and optimisation of assistance to people who come into contact with the justice system.

Foundation, set up by students, higher education and the Ministry of OCW, that collects and distributes objective study choice information on hbo and wo programmes. It runs the Nationale Studenten Enquête every year.

Network organisation of addiction care institutions with probation recognition, alongside Reclassering Nederland and Leger des Heils Jeugdbescherming & Reclassering. It supervises suspects and convicts with addictions and advises the court and the Public Prosecution Service. The Reclasseringsregeling 1995 governs recognition.

Foundation, established on 10-05-2000, that offers recognition and support to veterans and their families, issues veteran cards and insignia, and organises Veterans Day. The Veteranenloket is the service point for care from Defence, ABP and other partners.

Non-profit foundation that, under the Wet aansprakelijkheidsverzekering motorrijtuigen, compensates traffic victims when the party at fault is unknown, uninsured or the insurer is bankrupt. A surcharge on motor vehicle liability premiums funds it.
Independent foundation, set up in 1983, that guarantees loans of housing corporations so they can borrow at lower interest. WSW also monitors the financial health of affiliated corporations.

Foundation, set up at the end of 2011, that as an independent legal entity carries the academic education and research of the Faculty of Military Sciences of the Netherlands Defence Academy. It provides bachelor and master programmes under the higher education and research act.

Legal entity with a statutory task that carries out the health care scheme for military personnel on behalf of Defence. Military personnel in active service are exempt from the Zorgverzekeringswet and must be insured with the SZVK.

One of two recognised hallmarking institutions in the Netherlands, based in Gouda. It tests items of platinum, gold, palladium and silver for fineness and applies hallmarks under the Waarborgwet 2019. The Minister designates the institution.

Organisations that carry out the Wet langdurige zorg. The Minister designates one Wlz-uitvoerder per region as zorgkantoor. It contracts care providers, ensures clients receive the care they are entitled to and provides personal budgets.

Health insurers that provide the basic insurance that everyone aged 18 and over in the Netherlands must take out. The Zorgverzekeringswet requires them to accept every applicant for basic insurance, with no premium differences by health or age.

Independent administrative body under the Ministry of Justice and Security, set up in 1976 under the Wet schadefonds geweldsmisdrijven. It awards financial compensation to victims of serious violent and sexual crimes who suffer lasting harm. A commission of independent members sets policy.
Main advisory council for government and parliament on socio-economic issues, with employers, employees and independent Crown members.
Independent planning bureau that monitors, explains and explores the quality of life and society in the Netherlands.

Agency of the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations, a revenue-and-expenditure agency since 01-01-2013. SSC-ICT provides IT services and service desks to central government staff at home and abroad. The Regeling agentschappen sets its financing and governance.

Independent supervisor of mineral extraction and energy production, under the Ministry of Climate and Green Growth. It oversees safety of people and the environment in gas and geothermal extraction, among others. Its tasks are set in the Mijnbouwwet and the Gaswet.

Representative body (parliament) of the country of Aruba, elected by the residents for four years (Statuut art. 46; gobierno.aw). 21 seats, after the election of 06-12-2024: AVP 9, MEP 8, FUTURO Aruba 3, PPA 1. The parliamentary year starts on the second Tuesday of September.

Representative body (parliament) of the country of Curaçao, 21 members, elected at the election of 21-03-2025 and installed on 11-05-2025. Composition: MFK 13, PNP 4, PAR 2, MAN 2. The Staten scrutinise the government and hold it to account (parlamento.cw).

Representative body (parliament) of the country of Sint Maarten, 15 elected members (sxmparliament.org). Established on 10-10-2010, the day on which the country of Sint Maarten gained status equalis within the Kingdom.

Part of the Directorate for Service Delivery, Partnerships and Implementation of the Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment. It carries out (European) subsidy schemes, such as ESF+, and other complex assignments in the field of work and income.
